content.content:
# BUILD HOST — all builds and heavy dev work run on node-2, not the primary

**Since 2026-10-07 (owner decision).** The primary (ns5002569, 51.79.162.96) only serves the live site:
prod web/worker, Postgres, customer VMs. Parallel agent builds there pushed load to 16+, filled swap
and hard-crashed it on 2026-10-06. Everything heavy now runs on **node-2 = nxeon-fsn1
(178.63.94.114)**, inside a capped systemd slice.

Full technical write-up: `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` → "Build host (node-2)".

## What runs where

| Work | Where | How |
|---|---|---|
| Production / staging release builds (`npm install`, `prisma generate`, `next build`) | node-2, `nxeon-build-prod.slice` | automatically by `scripts/promote-production.sh` / `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` |
| Schema push, pre-cutover smoke (:3095), cutover, restarts, rollback | primary | same scripts, unchanged |
| Agent `tsc`, tests, `next build`, `next dev`, Playwright, throwaway DBs | node-2, `nxeon-build-agents.slice` | `scripts/devhost` (below) |
| Editing files, git commits | primary, in **your own worktree** | as before |

## Caps on node-2 (it also runs ~13 customer VMs — never touch them)

- `nxeon.slice` CPUWeight 20 / IOWeight 10 (VMs in `qemu.slice` win any contention ~5:1)
- `nxeon-build.slice`: **CPUQuota 900 % (9 of 12 threads, raised 2026-10-08), MemoryMax 10 G, MemoryHigh 9.5 G, no swap**
  - `nxeon-build-prod.slice`: release builds — CPUWeight 1000, MemoryLow 6 G, oom_score_adj 500
  - `nxeon-build-agents.slice`: agent work — **MemoryMax 7 G**, oom_score_adj 1000 (dies first)
- every process: nice 10, ionice best-effort 7. Build files live on `tank` (separate SATA SSD);
  VMs are on `rpool` (NVMe), so build IO never hits their disks.
- **Build lock** on node-2: `/run/lock/nxeon-build.lock` — one heavy job at a time
  (release builds, `devhost build|test`, `devhost run --lock`). Locked agent jobs are capped at
  25 min by default so a promote (waits max 30 min) is never starved.

## How agents work from now on

1. Make your own worktree on the primary (never work in `/opt/nxeon` or `/opt/nxeon-staging`):
   `git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main`
   You do NOT need `node_modules` in it (and never symlink one in).
2. Edit with your normal tools. Then, from inside the worktree, run heavy things on node-2:
   ```
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost tsc                    # npx tsc --noEmit
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost test [test/x.test.ts]  # tsx --test (takes the build lock)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost build                  # next build (takes the build lock)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost run -- <cmd...>        # anything else; add --lock if heavy
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost db push                # schema into YOUR throwaway DB
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost dev                    # next dev on node-2 127.0.0.1:<port>
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost tunnel <port>          # reach it from the primary (curl/Playwright)
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost run -- npx playwright test ...   # or run Playwright ON node-2
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost pull <path> [dest]     # copy screenshots/reports back
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost stop [name|all]        # ALWAYS stop dev servers when done
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost rm                     # when finished: units, DB and node-2 copy gone
   /opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost status                 # node-2 load, slice memory, lock, running units
   ```
   Each command mirrors your worktree's source (git-tracked + untracked-not-ignored; never
   `.git`, `node_modules`, `.next`, `.env*`) to `/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>` on node-2, installs
   deps there when `package-lock.json`/schema changed, and runs the command in the agents slice.
   The node-2 copy is disposable — commit in your primary worktree only.
3. **Throwaway database**: every workspace gets its own `wt_<name>` on node-2's private Postgres
   cluster (`127.0.0.1:5433`, role `nxeon_agent`, never exposed). `DATABASE_URL`, a random
   `AUTH_SECRET`, `APP_URL`, `PORT` are preset. Extra non-secret env: `devhost env set K=V` (it
   refuses any value that is a live prod/staging value). **Agents never need, and must never use,
   production DB credentials.**
4. Only if node-2 is down: say so to the owner. Do not fall back to building on the primary.

## Forbidden (hard rules)

- **No `next build`, full test suites, dev servers, Playwright or JDKs on the primary.** Use devhost.
- **Never run `REASSIGN OWNED`, `DROP OWNED`, `ALTER ... OWNER`, `CREATE/ALTER/DROP ROLE`, or any
  database-ownership command** — on any cluster, including node-2's throwaway one.
- **Never `pkill`/`killall` by pattern** (`next`, `node`, `npm`, ...): it hits prod/staging too.
  Stop by unit (`devhost stop`) or by the PID on your own port.
- **Never `git add -A` / `git add .`** — add only the files you changed.
- Never touch customer VMs (`qm`, `qemu.slice`) on node-2; never raise the slice caps.
- Never copy a production `.env` (or any secret) to node-2. Never print secrets.
- Never build in `/opt/nxeon` or `/opt/nxeon-staging`; never `git checkout` there.

## Deploys (owner/root only)

`scripts/deploy-staging.sh [ref]` → verify → `scripts/promote-production.sh` — unchanged usage;
the build now happens on node-2 automatically. `--build-local` = emergency fallback (old on-box
build) if node-2 is unreachable. Rollback unchanged: `scripts/rollback-release.sh --production`.

## Admin

- Re-provision / refresh node-2 (idempotent): `scripts/buildhost/provision.sh` (ships the
  primary's exact Node toolchain to `/opt/nxeon-build/node`, re-applies slices, datasets, mirror,
  Postgres). Run it after upgrading Node on the primary — promotes refuse a version mismatch.
- Release build log on node-2: `/tank/nxeon-deploy/<env>/build.log`.

content.content:
# Cyrus token economy (design, 2026-10-07)

Branch `feature/cyrus-tokens` (worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-cyrustokens`). Code: `lib/cyrus/tokens/*`.
Every number below is an admin Setting (`cyrus_tok_*`, editable at `/admin/cyrus-tokens`); the
values here are the shipped defaults (`lib/cyrus/tokens/config.ts`). Nothing in this file is a
forecast of customer behaviour: the cost figures are measured builds, the rest are rules.

## 0. The data this is built on

| Source | What | Numbers |
|---|---|---|
| `/root/agent-notes/modbuilder-preview/phase0-builds.jsonl` | 10 real builds, Sonnet 5, pre-tuning | avg $0.28, $0.08-$0.47 |
| docs "AI Mod Builder: tuning" eval (28 prompts) | service 0.3, Sonnet 5.5 | avg $0.104 / median $0.097; simple $0.066, standard $0.102, complex $0.189 |
| same eval, Haiku on simple | Haiku 4.5 | $0.118/build (more turns than Sonnet 5.5), 1/8 failed |
| build service records on VM 88001 (138 builds, read-only) | auto-routed + Cyrus tiers | Haiku-only auto builds avg $0.068 (n=7); Sonnet 5.5 auto avg $0.104 (n=28) |
| Cyrus tier builds (same records) | `tier` set | Katara ChunkMirror change $0.159; Saka ChunkMirror fresh $0.676 (443 s, Sonnet 5); Saka others $0.055 / $0.304; Yakko SimpleHeal $0.341 (Opus 5) |
| ChunkMirror pre-tuning (auto, Sonnet) | | $0.217 |
| Anthropic list prices (per MTok in/out) | | Haiku 4.5 $1/$5 · Sonnet 5 and 5.5 $2/$10 · Opus 5 $5/$25 |
| Refusals (adversarial prompts) | | $0.005-$0.028 |

Two findings the owner should know (not changed by this work, see Owner decisions):
- **Saka maps to Sonnet 5, not 5.5** (`MB_TIER_SAKA`). The tuned default routing uses 5.5, which
  was cheaper, faster and more reliable in the eval. The one Saka-tier ChunkMirror cost $0.676,
  3x the auto-routed one.
- **Katara (Haiku 4.5) is not cheaper per build than Sonnet 5.5** on simple mods ($0.118 vs
  $0.061 in the eval), because it takes about twice the turns. The economy still prices tokens
  on the real cost, so this only affects how much a Katara build spends, never the margin.

## 1. What a token is

**1 token = $0.002 of measured AI cost** (`cyrus_tok_tokens_per_usd = 500`), times a per-model
multiplier: Katara x1.0, Saka x1.0, **Yakko x1.25** (Opus runs vary more and hold a build slot
about twice as long). A build that reached the AI costs at least 5 tokens (`cyrus_tok_min_spend`).

    tokens charged = max(5, ceil(costUsd x 500 x multiplier[model]))

`costUsd` is the build service's own number for that build (`ModBuild.costUsd`). The token is a
*cost* unit, so margin lives entirely in what a token *sells* for (section 3), and Yakko costing
many more tokens than Katara falls out of the real costs (Opus is 5x Haiku per token).

### Tokens per typical build

| Model | Typical (measured) | Tokens | Big build | Tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Katara | simple $0.068 (auto Haiku avg) | **34** | ChunkMirror change $0.159 | **80** |
| Saka | $0.104 (Sonnet 5.5 avg) / $0.189 complex | **52** / 95 | Sonnet 5 tier: $0.30 / $0.676 | 150 / 338 |
| Yakko | simple $0.341 (measured) | **214** | complex ~$1.18 (Opus 2.5x Sonnet 5 complex $0.47, extrapolated) | ~738 |

Pre-build estimate shown in the composer (`cyrus_tok_reserve_table`, tokens, [typical, high]):

| | simple | standard | complex |
|---|---|---|---|
| Katara | 30-70 | 60-140 | 100-240 |
| Saka | 35-100 | 60-220 | 110-400 |
| Yakko | 100-250 | 200-500 | 400-1000 |

Complexity comes from the existing `lib/cyrus/estimate.ts` feature count (unchanged).

## 2. Game-server grants

    per-month amount = clamp(round5(base + perUsd x monthly price $), min, max)
    initial:  base 100, perUsd 16, min 150, max 750
    renewal:  base 25,  perUsd 6,  min 40,  max 300

`monthly price` = what the customer actually paid per month (after coupons/partner discount,
before tax). Prepaid terms: an N-month purchase gets initial + renewal x (N-1); an N-month
renewal gets renewal x N; N capped at 12 (`cyrus_tok_grant_term_months_cap`).

| Monthly price | Initial | AI cost if all used (% of 1st month) | Every renewal | (% of renewal) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $2.99 | 150 | $0.30 (10.0%) | 45 | $0.09 (3.0%) |
| $4.99 | 180 | $0.36 (7.2%) | 55 | $0.11 (2.2%) |
| $8.99 | 245 | $0.49 (5.5%) | 80 | $0.16 (1.8%) |
| $9.99 | **260** | $0.52 (5.2%) | 85 | $0.17 (1.7%) |
| $15.99 | 355 | $0.71 (4.4%) | 120 | $0.24 (1.5%) |
| $30.00 | 580 | $1.16 (3.9%) | 205 | $0.41 (1.4%) |
| $49.99+ | 750 (cap) | $1.50 | 300 (cap) | $0.60 |

Owner's example check: a ~$10 server gives 260 tokens. ChunkMirror on Katara measured 80 tokens
($0.159); even the pre-tuning $0.217 ChunkMirror is 109 tokens. Either way more than half is left

content.thinking:
Since the gate text for a change combines the base prompt with the change request, the complexity—and thus the reserve cost—ends up roughly matching the original mod's range rather than being smaller for edits. But actual spend tends to run around 0.8x of a fresh build cost, so I need to reconcile that gap when estimating how many edits a given reserve can support.

Checking against measured data though, this assumption breaks down — Katara's ChunkMirror edit cost more tokens than a simple mod, so edits aren't inherently cheaper. I'll just define edit cost as simple-mod cost times the 0.8 change factor and compute count ranges from token budgets, accepting that the resulting ranges are wide and should be displayed as approximate figures (e.g., "about 10 to 25 small mods, 5 to 12 typical mods, or 13 to 31 edits"), possibly rounding for readability.

I'm also thinking through how to display model access per plan tier — showing compact per-model rows with glyphs for unlocked models (e.g., Saka plan shows ranges for both Katara and Saka). Before writing any of this up, I want to review the relevant files first: the modbuilder types, real.ts, the Versions/Notes tabs, BranchOverview, the icon kit components, tokens.css, and the existing CyrusBadge component used elsewhere.

import math, json
def f(x): 
    s=f"{x:.2f}".rstrip("0").rstrip(".")
    return "0" if s in ("-0","") else s
def comma(R, r, phi_deg, theta_deg, cx=12, cy=12):
    th=math.radians(theta_deg); phi=math.radians(phi_deg)
    u=(math.cos(th), math.sin(th))
    Pout=(cx+R*u[0], cy+R*u[1])
    p=R-2*r
    Pin=(cx+p*u[0], cy+p*u[1])
    T=(cx+R*math.cos(th-phi), cy+R*math.sin(th-phi))
    s=(2*p*R*math.cos(phi)-p*p-R*R)/(2*(p-R*math.cos(phi)))
    rho=abs(s)
    large_outer = 1 if phi>math.pi else 0
    # outer arc from T to Pout increasing angle (sweep=1 in SVG y-down = clockwise visually = increasing angle)
    d=f"M{f(T[0])} {f(T[1])}A{f(R)} {f(R)} 0 {large_outer} 1 {f(Pout[0])} {f(Pout[1])}"
    # head semicircle from Pout to Pin, continuing the same rotation direction
    d+=f"A{f(r)} {f(r)} 0 0 1 {f(Pin[0])} {f(Pin[1])}"
    # inner arc back to T (concave)
    d+=f"A{f(rho)} {f(rho)} 0 0 0 {f(T[0])} {f(T[1])}Z"
    return d

json.dump(out,open("paths.json","w"),indent=1)

def svg(k,variant,size=96):
    g=grads[k]
    paths=out[k]
    if variant=="gradient":
        body=f'<defs><linearGradient id="g" x1="4" y1="3" x2="20" y2="21" gradientUnits="userSpaceOnUse"><stop offset="0" stop-color="{g[0]}"/><stop offset=".5" stop-color="{g[1]}"/><stop offset="1" stop-color="{g[2]}"/></linearGradient></defs>'
        body+=f'<circle cx="12" cy="12" r="10.6" fill="none" stroke="url(#g)" stroke-width="1.2" opacity=".55"/>'

        body+="".join(f'<path d="{d}" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity=".22" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linejoin="round"/>' for d in paths)
    return f'<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="{size}" height="{size}" color="#e9e3ff">{body}</svg>'
for k in out:

content.content:
#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# devhost — run agent dev work on the BUILD HOST (node-2), not on the primary.
#
# Edit files on the primary as usual (your own git worktree — never /opt/nxeon),
# then run every heavy command through this helper. It mirrors your worktree's
# source to node-2 (/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>, own node_modules there), runs the
# command inside the capped nxeon-build-agents.slice with a THROWAWAY database
# (Postgres on node-2 127.0.0.1:5433), and streams the output back.
#
#   scripts/devhost run [--lock] [--max SEC] -- CMD...   push + run CMD in the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost tsc                                  = run -- npx tsc --noEmit
#   scripts/devhost test [FILES...]                      = run --lock -- npx tsx --test ...
#   scripts/devhost build                                = run --lock -- npx next build
#   scripts/devhost dev [--port P]                       start `next dev` on node-2 (background unit)
#   scripts/devhost bg NAME [--port P] -- CMD...         any background process (worker, preview server)
#   scripts/devhost stop [NAME|all]                      stop this worktree's background units
#   scripts/devhost logs [NAME] [-n N] [-f]              journal of a background unit (default: dev)
#   scripts/devhost tunnel PORT [LOCAL_PORT]             ssh -L so the primary can curl/Playwright it
#   scripts/devhost pull REMOTE_PATH [LOCAL_DEST]        copy results (screenshots, reports) back
#   scripts/devhost push                                 just sync files (run does this itself)
#   scripts/devhost install                              force npm install + prisma generate there
#   scripts/devhost db push|reset|info                   throwaway DB: schema push / recreate / name
#   scripts/devhost env set KEY=VALUE | unset KEY | list extra env for this worktree (never prod secrets)
#   scripts/devhost rm                                   stop units, drop the throwaway DB, delete the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost ls | status | sync                   workspaces / node-2 load / push refs to node-2's mirror
#
# Rules: /root/agent-notes/BUILD-HOST.md. The node-2 copy is a build/run sandbox,
# not a place to edit or commit — your primary-side worktree stays the source of truth.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
# shellcheck source=lib/buildhost-env.sh
source "$HERE/lib/buildhost-env.sh"
REPO="${DEVHOST_REPO:-/opt/nxeon}"
die() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
say() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; }
q() { printf '%q ' "$@"; }
# ---- workspace identity -----------------------------------------------------
worktree_root() {
  local top; top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || die "run this inside your own git worktree of the Nxeon repo"
  top=$(readlink -f "$top")
  case "$top" in
    /opt/nxeon|/opt/nxeon-staging|/tank/nxeon-deploy/*) die "$top is a live/deploy tree. Create your own worktree first:  git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main" ;;
  esac
  [ -L "$top/.next" ] && die "$top/.next is a symlink (a live tree) — refusing"
  [ -L "$top/node_modules" ] && say "warning: $top/node_modules is a symlink — never 'git add -A' here (see BUILD-HOST.md). devhost does not need local node_modules at all."
  echo "$top"
}
ws_name() {
  local top="$1" n
  n=$(basename "$top" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | tr -c 'a-z0-9-\n' '-' | sed -E 's/-+/-/g; s/^-//; s/-$//' | cut -c1-40)
  [ -n "$n" ] || n=wt
  echo "${DEVHOST_NAME:-$n}"
}
init_ws() {
  TOP=$(worktree_root); NAME=$(ws_name "$TOP")
  case "$NAME" in *[!a-z0-9-]*|"") die "bad workspace name '$NAME' (DEVHOST_NAME=...)";; esac
  WS="$BH_ROOT/wt/$NAME"
  ENVF="/etc/nxeon-build/wt/$NAME.env"
  DBNAME="wt_$(echo "$NAME" | tr '-' '_')"
  PORT=$(( 4100 + $(printf '%s' "$NAME" | cksum | cut -d' ' -f1) % 800 ))
}
# Create the node-2 side once: dir, owner marker, throwaway DB, env file.
ensure_remote() {
  bh_ssh "bash -s" <<EOF >&2
set -euo pipefail
[ "\$(hostname)" = "$BUILD_HOST_NAME" ] || { echo "not node-2" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p $(q "$WS") /etc/nxeon-build/wt; chmod 700 /etc/nxeon-build/wt
mk=$(q "$WS/.devhost-owner")
if [ -f "\$mk" ] && [ "\$(cat "\$mk")" != $(q "$TOP") ]; then
  echo "workspace $NAME belongs to \$(cat "\$mk") — set DEVHOST_NAME=<unique> for $TOP" >&2; exit 1
fi
printf '%s\n' $(q "$TOP") > "\$mk"
. /etc/nxeon-build/agents-db.env
if [ ! -s $(q "$ENVF") ]; then
  sec=\$(head -c 48 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' | head -c 48)

content.content:
### Cyrus v5: the owner's redesign (2026-10-08, branch `feature/cyrus-v5`)

The owner's own Cyrus redesign (handoff `/tank/handoffs/cyrus/cyrus-handoff/`, START-HERE.md) replaces the v4 studio at **`/dashboard/cyrus`** (+ `/dashboard/cyrus/[id]`, and the core gallery at **`/dashboard/cyrus/cores`**). Same preview gate (`requireModBuilderUser()` on every page, `modBuilderUser()` on every API). The portal sidebar and top bar stay; the studio fills the app frame.

**Where it lives.** UI `components/cyrus/{chrome,cosmos,cores,icons,preview,prompt}` + `CyrusApp.tsx` (handoff components, imports re-rooted); state/engine `lib/cyrus/{store,forge,fx,data,types,camera,hooks,zip,highlight}.ts` + `lib/cyrus/engine/` (template generators); game logos `public/cyrus/games/`. Kept from v4: `components/cyrus/kit/` (icon set used by the token modal, the install-to-server modal), `lib/cyrus/{projects,meta,models,estimate,uploads,diff,tokens/}`.

**Scoping (nothing leaks into the portal).** `app/dashboard/cyrus/layout.tsx` wraps every Cyrus route in `.cyrus-root.nx-dark-island` and loads Inter / Space Grotesk / JetBrains Mono as CSS variables on that box only. `studio.css` (handoff globals + network CSS) and `cores/cores.css` are generated from the handoff with every selector under `.cyrus-root`, keyframes and `@property` renamed `cy5-*`, and the three class names that collide with portal globals renamed (`cy5-glass`, `cy5-btn-ghost`, `cy5-kbd`). The root uses `container-type: size; contain: layout paint`, so the handoff's `position: fixed` chrome is contained in the content area; `100vw/vh` became `cqw/cqh`. Tailwind colour tokens are `cy-*` (`text-cy-ink`, `border-cy-line` …, `@theme inline` in `app/globals.css` pointing at variables that exist only on `.cyrus-root`), plus a `cy-light:` variant. `nx-dark-island` keeps the portal's generated light-mode retargeting off the studio (it has its own light theme). `test/cyrus.test.ts` fails if a studio selector is unscoped or a keyframe isn't `cy5-`.

**Theme.** The portal's: `html[data-theme="light"]` / localStorage `nx-theme`. The studio's toggle presses the portal's own toggle button; `useCyrusBoot` mirrors `data-theme` into the store for the canvas and shaders. No `cyrus-theme` key.

**Real vs template.** Minecraft is the one real game (`GAMES[].real`). The account's builds are its Minecraft mods (`lib/cyrus/real.ts deriveReal`: one mod per project, builds = versions, category from the build's own words, at most two extra category branches). Minecraft seeds are dashed **ideas**: clicking one writes a buildable prompt. Notes / restore / favourite are the existing `PATCH /api/mod-builder/projects/:root`; files load lazily from `/api/mod-builder/builds/:id/source`; downloads are the real `.jar` / source zip; **Deploy** opens the v4 install modal. Every other game (and added games) is the handoff's template generator, labelled "Template preview", spends no tokens, kept in localStorage per account (`cyrus-state-v1:<userId>`).

**Forge stream** (`POST /api/cyrus/generate`, NDJSON, handoff §6 GenEvents). A prompt that routes to Minecraft, or a change to a real mod, goes through `lib/modbuilder/create.ts createModBuild` (extracted from `POST /api/mod-builder/builds`, which now calls it too: same validation, rate limits, 2-in-flight cap and token gate); token errors answer JSON 402/403/429 before the stream so `cyrusTokens.handleBuildError` opens the modal. Then `lib/cyrus/follow.ts` streams the real build: stage changes → `think`, the service `/live` draft → `file`/`chunk`, in-place edits → `file-set`, keep-alive `ping`, final source + `done {tokens: charged}` or `error`. `GET ?follow=<id>` re-attaches (page load with a running build, dropped connection; the client retries 4×). Template games run the handoff's `forgeStream()` (no model call). Additive event types: `build`, `file-set`, `ping`.

# Cyrus v6 studio-ui: notes (branch feature/cyrus-v6-studio)

## v4b (feature/cyrus-v5~2) -> v5 regressions

| Feature (v4b) | v5 state | v6 studio-ui |
|---|---|---|
| Explain tab (plain English, how to use, commands, settings, permissions, good to know) | gone (only markdown in Notes) | RESTORED (`preview/ExplainTab.tsx`) |
| Safety check panel (4 guarantees, findings, pill) | one line in notes | RESTORED (Explain) |
| Failure reasons per error code, compiler output | raw error only | RESTORED (Explain + Code tab) |
| Try again / Edit and retry | missing | RESTORED (`lib/cyrus/retry.ts`) |
| Request quote, original description, attachment thumbnails | missing | RESTORED (Explain) |
| Diff / compare versions (DiffView) | missing (lib/cyrus/diff.ts unused) | RESTORED: Versions > Compare (unified diff) |
| Rename project | missing | RESTORED (pencil / double-click title) |
| Favourite | missing | RESTORED (star, real projects) |
| Share / copy link | missing (URL synced only) | RESTORED (link button) |
| Built with Cyrus badge | not rendered | Explain footer (`BuiltWithCyrusBadge`) |
| Keyboard shortcuts `?` sheet, N, F, V, 1-5 | only Ctrl K, /, Esc | NOT restored (added E = expand). Left. |
| Version lanes / branch from a version | timeline only | NOT restored. Left. |
| File search + "Ask Cyrus" in the palette | games/categories/mods/actions | NOT restored. Left. |
| Queue position + "fix N of 3" in the live view | missing | NOT restored. Left. |
| Screenshot capture (getDisplayMedia), voice V key + level meter | missing | NOT restored. Left. |
| Model-advice nudge ("Katara is light for this") | missing | NOT restored. Left. |
| NxLabs "View on NxLabs" / publish teaser | missing | community agent |
| Server Mods tab enable/disable | never in studio | lifecycle agent |

## Decisions taken (owner can overturn)

- Add game: only games in the Cyrus registry or with a ring preset, not on the ring. Only games with a
  generator can be added; registry-only (ARK, The Isle) show "Coming soon" and can't be added. Today all
  six supported games are on the ring, so the dashed branch, top-bar button, overview button and
  palette action are hidden. Custom branches made before v6 are kept (removable).
- Template-game demo mods removed from the studio (coordinator/owner decision); kept in
  `lib/cyrus/demo-seeds.ts` for the marketing demo (`useStore.setState({ demo: true })`).
- Minecraft idea seeds kept, but opening one no longer shows template code as if it were built.
- Expanded panel: desktop leaves the dock usable below it; phones get a full-screen sheet.
- Favicon: a vector rebuild of the black-tile pick (the owner's rule: chrome marks are SVG), PNG only for
  apple-touch/192.
- Rail highlight: one treatment in both themes, because the portal rail stays dark in light mode.

## Owner decisions still open

- Cyrus avatar (`CYRUS_AVATAR_ASSET` = iconset-r2-1 for now).
- Model glyph direction (crystal tier: 1/2/3 crystals). If rejected, only the paths in
  `components/cyrus/icons/ModelGlyphs.tsx` + `public/cyrus/models/*` change.
- Edits estimate assumes an edit costs 0.8x a small mod (CHANGE_COST_FACTOR). The economy notes say one
  measured Katara change cost more than a typical small build; a measured change factor would sharpen it.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

input.message:
**studio-ui: Cyrus v6 studio fixes are done; the fixes after the first screenshot round are not yet re-screenshotted.**

Branch `feature/cyrus-v6-studio`, worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-v6-studio`. Two commits: `2dc9d913ba` and `423f553388`. Nothing is merged or deployed.

`.cyrus-verify/` (seed, local stand-in for the build service, Playwright script) is an untracked throwaway and must not be committed.

**What I built**

1. **One core.** The `/dashboard/cyrus/cores` route, the Cores button, the palette entry, the `coreStyle` state and the nine other core concepts are deleted. Particle Nebula is the only core; its renderer is unchanged.
2. **Hierarchy legend** removed.
3. **Add game.** The dialog only lists supported games. A game can be added only if Cyrus has a generator for it; ARK and The Isle show "Coming soon" but can't be added (logic in `lib/cyrus/ring.ts`). All six supported games are already on the ring, so the dashed branch, top-bar button, overview button and palette action are hidden. The free-text custom game form is gone; branches added before v6 stay and can still be removed.
4. **Expandable preview panel.** A button or `E` expands it, `Esc` collapses it first, and the choice is remembered. On desktop it takes most of the stage with the prompt dock below; at 390 px it becomes a full-screen sheet.
5. **Explain tab** (restored from v4b). For real builds: a plain-English summary, how to use it, commands, settings, permissions, the safety scan, limits, the request with its images, and for failed builds the reason, tips, compiler output and **Try again / Edit and retry**. Template mods get a generated explanation labelled "Template preview".
6. **Model picker** is now opaque in dark and light, with a clear selected state, typical tokens per build, and locked rows that open the plans.
7. **New model glyphs** for Katara, Saka and Yakko: one, two and three crystals, in gradient and mono versions. They are a React component (`components/cyrus/icons/ModelGlyphs.tsx`) and files (`public/cyrus/models/*.svg`), used in the picker, dock, trace, plans and token chip.
